Delhi‑Haridwar Expressway to Cut Journey to 90 Minutes, Minister Says

New Expressway Promises a 90‑Minute Delhi‑Haridwar Trip

Union Road Transport and Highways Minister Nitin Gadkari announced that a dedicated expressway linking Delhi and Haridwar could be completed within the next two months. When operational, the route is expected to reduce the current three‑to‑four‑hour drive to roughly 1.5 hours, enabling a day‑trip itinerary that many pilgrims and tourists have long desired.

Official Statement and Timeline

Speaking at the Confederation of Indian Industry’s (CII) National Conference on the Future of India, Gadkari said the expressway would be ready “in the next two months.” No specific opening date was given, and the announcement did not include a detailed construction schedule or a formal inauguration plan.

How the Expressway Fits Into Recent Road Improvements

The Delhi‑Haridwar project follows the recent launch of the Delhi‑Dehradun Greenfield Expressway, which cut travel time between the two cities from five‑to‑six hours down to about two hours. Gadkari highlighted similar reductions on other corridors:

  • Delhi‑Meerut: from ~3.5 hours to 45‑50 minutes.
  • Delhi‑Jaipur: from ~5 hours to 2 hours.
  • Bengaluru‑Chennai: from ~4‑5 hours to ~2 hours.

These examples illustrate a broader push to upgrade India’s road network, which the minister says is helping lower logistics costs and boost economic activity.

Economic and Tourism Implications

Pilgrimage Tourism

Haridwar is a major pilgrimage destination on the Ganga. A 90‑minute drive would allow visitors to leave Delhi early, perform a river dip, and have breakfast in Haridwar on the same day. Gadkari linked this improvement to the Char Dham project, noting that about 85 % of that Rs 12,000‑crore initiative is complete and that travel from Delhi to Badrinath and Kedarnath has already tripled.

Logistics Costs

Gadkari cited a decline in India’s logistics cost share of GDP—from 16 % to ~9 %—attributing part of the reduction to new road infrastructure. For comparison, he mentioned China’s logistics cost at 8 % of GDP and the United States at 12 %.

Employment and Development

The minister suggested that capital expenditure in tourism‑related infrastructure could generate new jobs, though no specific employment figures were provided.

Uncertainties and What Remains Unclear

  • Exact Completion Date: The “two‑month” timeline lacks a concrete date, and no progress reports have been released since the announcement.
  • Funding and Cost Details: While Gadkari referenced a broader Rs 1.6 lakh crore road‑infrastructure program for Delhi, the specific budget for the Delhi‑Haridwar expressway was not disclosed.
  • Operational Details: Information on tolls, lane count, design speed, and environmental clearances was not mentioned.
  • Impact on Existing Routes: The article does not clarify how the new expressway will integrate with the existing NH 58 or whether it will replace or supplement it.

Practical Implications for Travelers

  • Potential Day‑Trip: If the expressway opens as projected, travelers could schedule a same‑day pilgrimage or leisure visit to Haridwar without overnight accommodation.
  • Cost Considerations: Until toll rates are announced, the overall cost of the shorter journey remains unknown.
  • Alternative Routes: Until the expressway is operational, the current NH 58 remains the primary route, with travel times of three to four hours depending on traffic.

How to Verify the Announcement

The statements quoted here are taken from Gadkari’s remarks at the CII conference, reported by India Today on 28 October 2026. Readers can review the original article at: https://www.indiatoday.in/cities/delhi/story/delhi-haridwar-expressway-90-minute-travel-nitin-gadkari-3026628-2026-10-28

Summary

The proposed Delhi‑Haridwar expressway promises a dramatic cut in travel time, aligning with a series of recent highway upgrades that have already shortened journeys across northern and southern India. While the minister’s optimism underscores the government’s focus on infrastructure as a catalyst for tourism, logistics savings, and employment, key details such as the exact opening date, toll structure, and integration with existing roads remain to be clarified.

--- *This article is based solely on the verified statements released by Union Minister Nitin Gadkari and reported by India Today. No additional sources were consulted.*
